scope: Categories 1 and 3 only; current pixels/spec, no earlier critic reports, prior scores, build recipes, repair plans or handoff narrative read.

3.name: Inspection/check-in hero hierarchy and functional composition

defects.title: Check-in is readable when faced, but weakly announced from the straight inspection approach

witnesses.region: left 0–29% of frame, office glazing and wall; forward scanner center
witnesses.observation: The actual hatch is outside the image; the forward yellow route and scanner are immediately legible, but the office side presents glazing without a readable check-in invitation.

witnesses.region: left third, counter and broad reassurance panel above it
witnesses.observation: The hatch becomes clear in this offset wide view; the largest text says WE VALUE YOUR TIME rather than identifying the required check-in function.
The return lane remains obvious, but the hatch is again absent from the forward view.

witnesses.region: left/front of cutaway, orange dashed branch toward counter
witnesses.observation: The small check-in floor branch is visible in the overhead audit; it does not provide comparable identification in the enclosed entry view.

defects.impact: A worker can understand the straight inspection lane faster than the lateral check-in stop. This is a modest wayfinding and co-hero hierarchy weakness, not a claim of a blocked route or a required runtime sequence.
defects.repair: Reorient or improve the existing office-side check-in cue so it is readable from the preserved straight approach. Give the current hatch identification a clearer value/shape relationship to the reassurance panel, or replace part of that panel with a concise functional cue. Keep the counter, wall, door, room boundaries and route reservations fixed; do not add a forest of signs.

defects.title: Cart bypass depends on the shot label more than an in-world functional identifier

witnesses.region: center closed gate leaves; lower-left small control marked GATE; right mast dark upper plate
witnesses.observation: Manufactured gate leaves and controller are readable, but no comparably clear cart-only pictogram or function label identifies this adjacent lane at player distance. The bottom-left CART BYPASS text belongs to render evidence.

witnesses.region: right half, adjacent closed gate and parallel yellow floor lane
witnesses.observation: The personnel arch has a strong explicit name; the neighboring lane shares yellow route grammar and does not communicate its distinct cart role as immediately.

witnesses.region: right of arch, gate leaves and tall mast
witnesses.observation: Worker inspection is clear, while the adjacent gated function needs inference from width and construction.

defects.impact: The broad gate is not confused with the scanner aperture, but the intended cart function and lane distinction take longer to read than the strongly named personnel lane.
defects.repair: Use a small restrained cart pictogram or concise cart identifier on an existing gate/mast face, paired with its control, keeping all gate geometry, aperture, footprint and lane reservations unchanged. Prefer replacing an existing blank or generic plate to adding new signage.

overall_99_gate: Cannot evaluate with two categories. These scores are not an overall acceptance claim.
strengths: The worker arch gives a clear forward landmark in entry, approach and reverse views.
Inspection lanes and quiet return space remain legible; the cutaways show a coherent separation of office, inspection, service and concealed support areas.
Human scale is credible from doors, chair, counter and trolley. No obvious spatial scale failure or visually blocked principal route was found.
The counter is specific and strongly readable in its front/detail views, and the cargo machine remains recognizable in the cargo heroes.
Wall elevations show quiet surfaces and clear openings rather than distracting secondary prop competition.
limitations: Pixel review does not measure exact world clearances, hinge sweeps, physical support contact, collision or navigation. Native/technical review owns those checks.

Covered trolley visually occludes parts of the evidence fronts in HERO_EVIDENCE/HERO_TROLLEY; the pixels alone do not establish an access collision, so no access-critical defect or score deduction is asserted.
Cutaways and elevation views are used to audit layout and wall construction, not to certify enclosed atmosphere.
Neutral and UV images were opened and compared for assembly placement and silhouette. Material, UV, lighting and broader art veto judgments remain with their independent specialists.
No earlier cycle was read, so stability across cycles and cold-render comparison are not certified here.
release: All hash/decode file handles are closed. No Blender process or native/recipe-content reader was started. No native/recipe reader or process is retained. Source and recipes were not edited.
